saki_devotion_450_10.m: Kha'zaan are no more, thanks to you. Their spirits lingered, making us hide.

saki_devotion_480_10.m: Kha'zaan are no more. However, in the future, be wary, and learn not to get bamboozled. Hope you have learned your lesson.

saki_devotion_480_20.m: Anyways, it was their spirits that lingered, making us hide.

saki_devotion_480_ysrine_10.m: Aye, little one. What were you thinking?

saki_dominion_10.m: Well, now you need to find more spirits in this place. Ours.
r: And you want me to liberate them. Why?

saki_dominion_100.m: They will return again and again unless stopped. Kill them, reclaim the pearls, and bring them here.
r: I will return with the soul pearls.

saki_dominion_20.m: Because while the light of Elythara may not be extinguished, it has dimmed here in Dhayavar.
r: Why would your colleagues be spirits? You won the war.

saki_dominion_30.m: Did we win? Perhaps. Narrowly. And not decisively. The Shadow remains, and monsters from the other realm still roam freely.
r: They lost their bodies during the war?

saki_dominion_40.m: Yes. Five of my closest colleagues lost their corporeal forms here. The magic was heavy, and Elythara's blessing caused their spirits to linger.

saki_dominion_50.m: Er...yes. Similar. And now that the Kha'zaan are gone, they remain. Will you help them?

saki_dominion_60.m: They helped defend Dhayavar. They are not likely to harm any of us now.
r: Very well. What needs to be done?

saki_dominion_70.m: You are right to be wary. But I swear on Elythara, no harm will come from us.
r: Tell me what I must do.

saki_dominion_80.m: When they fell, their souls condensed into pearls. Five in total.

saki_dominion_90.m: Yes. Shimmering soul pearls. Liches gathered them, unaware of what they carried.
r: So I must destroy the liches and recover the pearls.

saki_fight_20.m: You can't have what is mine! I shall use this power to cleanse a corner of Dhayavar and make it my Dominion!
r: You followers of Kazaul - you want everything for yourself! Give them up!
[freaking out] Who are you? Where did you come from?

saki_meet_20.m: Saki, my name is. Haunt this area is all I do.

saki_not_5_pearls.m: You still have to find all of them. Now go.
r: Right, I need to find five of them.

saki_pearls_10.m: Are you returning because you were successful in retrieving the pearls?
r: [lie] Yes. Here you go, all five of them.

saki_pearls_20.m: Thank you for these powerful artifacts!

saki_trapped_10.m: I'm not able to get out!

saki_trapped_20.m: My barriers are not just physical, but magical. No one can enter or leave Undertell without my say so. $playername, get this guy!

ysrine_default_10.m: Oh, a human child, here? How did that come about?
r: Shannal let me through. Can I ask you, why do you look different than the others here?

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_10.m: Oh no. Just as I feared.

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_20.m: Like I feared. He was up to no good.

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_30.m: Saki seemed kind, even gentle. But there were inconsistencies in his stories. I assumed they came from the loss of memory that follows death. I was wrong.

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_40.m: Saki was no follower of Elythara. He sought to absorb the spirits of the Elytharan mages and draw power from them. I fear he serves the Kazaul, and he must be stopped.
r: By we, do you mean me?

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_60.m: Saki is trying to flee Undertell. Find him, defeat him, and recover the soul pearls and anything else he carries. Bring them back here.
r: Looks like no one can be trusted.

ysrine_dominion_saki_fleed_70.m: In the end, trust is still required. Without it, we would already be lost.

ysrine_heartstone_10.m: It is not ordinary ore. Heartstone drinks the breath of the Rift and holds it. They wanted it.

ysrine_heartstone_20.m: Long ago, the first King of Nor City, Garthan of House Houdart, sent men into Galmore to pry at the mountain. They prized what they pulled from the mountain, though few ever speak plainly of why.
r: What did they want it for?
Thank you. That is enough for now.

ysrine_heartstone_30.m: Power and profit are plain reasons. Old families in Nor City desired advantage. That is what men call progress and what others call cost. Remember this when you carry the stone.

ysrine_looks_10.m: This is what happened when he died [point to the man at the table]. That is what happened when they died [pointing east]. It's all very personal.

ysrine_question_coins_10.m: Oh, sorry, child. I am not knowledgeable about such things.

ysrine_questions_10.m: You carry questions like coins. Ask them, child.
r: What is this heartstone everyone speaks of?
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
I found these coins [showing Ysrine the rare coins] here in Undertell. Are you familiar with them?

ysrine_saki_killed_12.m: but unfortunately you've come empty handed. How did you manage to drop them on the way back?
r: Don't be so judgemental. They are really heavy, so I didn't want to carry them around with me.

ysrine_saki_killed_13.m: and you have brought the Soul pearls.
r: What do I do with the Soul pearls?

ysrine_saki_killed_14.m: Go get them and bring them back here!

ysrine_saki_killed_20.m:
Besides keeping them away from those Kazaul Masters? I do not know yet. Powerful they are - they could perhaps bring Elythara back, help her re-establish her Dominion on Dhayavar.
Those Pearls might be the key to bring Elythara back, and balance out the power of the five Masters. Let the wisdom of your travels guide you.

ysrine_saki_not_killed.m: This is no time to be fooling around. Please get those pearls back.

ysrine_start_devotion_10.m: Thank you! It's because of you that we are rid of the remnants of the Kha'zaan. On that note, there's someone here to meet you.

ysrine_undertell_after_arcir.m: Then you walk a quieter road than most.

ysrine_undertell_book_intro.m: Written histories come easily to stone and steel. They are less kind to breath, fear, and hunger.
r: It feels like something is missing.
A book collector from Fallhaven asked me to listen to the ghosts of Undertell.

ysrine_undertell_book_missing.m: What is measured can be counted. What is endured must be remembered. Undertell has little love for the latter.
r: You think the book leaves things out?

ysrine_undertell_omission.m: Those who suffered here were tools, not witnesses. Tools are used. Witnesses are avoided.
r: I should keep that in mind.

ysrine_undertell_quiet_road.m: The dead are accustomed to being spoken for. Few think to listen instead. Undertell remembers those who do.

ysrine_warn_of_master_lies_10.m: You have spoken with one of them, haven't you? Their words cling to you. Be careful what promises you keep down here.
r: They spoke of balance. I am not sure what they meant.
I did. Do you know what they want?
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
Actually, I want to talk about Saki.

ysrine_warn_of_master_lies_20.m: Balance can mean many things. For them, it once meant chains and silence. Listen closely, but never forget they speak for themselves, not for you.
r: I will keep that in mind.

ysrine_warn_of_master_lies_30.m: No one truly knows what the Masters want anymore. Even they may have forgotten. Just remember this: "truth and deceit sound much the same when spoken by the dead".
r: You sound like you don't trust them.

ysrine_warn_of_master_lies_40.m: Trust is for the living. Down here, it's better to doubt everything, even me.

fifth_master.10: In Undertell, the Kazaul Masters spoke to me. They claimed a forgotten ritual could seal the Rift once and for all.
fifth_master.20: They told me that this ritual was stolen long ago by a Lethgar named Varnel, who fled Undertell with it. I agreed to recover it, believing it might save Dhayavar.
fifth_master.30: In the upper dormitory tunnels of Undertell, I met the ghost of a miner who remembered Varnel. The ghost said Varnel escaped through the northern caverns and headed east toward the Sutdover River. Could he have meant Sullengard?
fifth_master.40: I traveled to Sullengard and spoke with Kealwea, the local priest. He recalled a relic matching my description once being sent to the Shadow church library in Remgard.
fifth_master.50: In Remgard's church basement, I spoke with Gwendolyn, the librarian. She said she knew nothing of any ritual but allowed me to search the shelves myself.
fifth_master.55: I discovered a small, locked box hidden behind the books. Its surface was etched with strange curling runes and old scorch marks. The box refused to open.
fifth_master.58: After I asked Gwendolyn about the locked box that I found, she directed me to speak with Skylenar upstairs.
fifth_master.60: Skylenar told me the box was an ancient relic, sealed by dragonkind and said to open only to a dragon's claw.
fifth_master.65: Skylenar mentioned that some old Shadow tales spoke of ash-covered scales found deep within Undertell, hinting that one such beast may once have lived there.
fifth_master.70: In the glowing white house basement, I talked to Falkour the dragon. When I showed him the locked box, he recognized it as a relic once held by Varnel.
fifth_master.72: Falkour gifted me one of his claws, saying it could break the seal, and warned me to use it only for that purpose. Time to find a safe place in this basement to open the box.
fifth_master.75: Using Falkour's claw, I unlocked the ancient box. Inside were the five pages of the Kazaul ritual the Masters desired.
fifth_master.78: The Master that I brought "The Five Aspects" ritual to sent me to talk to Thalen, the Master of Knowledge.
fifth_master.80: I returned the ritual to Thalen. He told me to meet the "lesser kin" at Anavrin's shrine to perform the ceremony.
fifth_master.85: As the ritual completed, the Masters revealed their true intent. The rite was not to seal the Rift but to awaken the Fifth Master, whose power might reopen it. They told me the Shadow itself serves Kazaul. Their words left me doubtful, unsure whether I had been deceived or warned.
fifth_master.90: I left Undertell uncertain of what to believe. If what the Masters said is true, the Shadow may not be what it seems. Still, doubt lingers like smoke after the forge cools.

devotion.20: Anoa told me that my presence in this cavern of Undertell had reawakened 11 shades of the Kha'zaan, who were dormant. I needed to eliminate them before they destroyed Dhayavar. It was their devotion to Kazaul which had preserved their existence till now.
devotion.30: I approached a Kha'zaan shade. But it was powerful enough to throw me out of the caverns and even out of Undertell. I needed to talk to Anoa.
devotion.40: Anoa told me to try again.
devotion.50: I again approached a shade. Again, I was thrown. Hope Anoa had a better alternative.
devotion.60: Anoa again told me to try harder.
devotion.70: Once more I was thrown out of the caverns the moment I approached a shade. This time, Anoa better help me in a smart way.
devotion.80: Anoa told me to pray to the statue of the Holy One in Sullengard square.
devotion.90: I prayed to the Holy One. I saw a ring at the foot of the statue.
devotion.100: I picked up the ring. I needed to get back to Anoa to learn how it works.
devotion.110: Anoa told me to wear it and approach the Kha'zaan shade.
devotion.120: A shade pleaded for mercy, promising a reward someday. I decided to let it go.
devotion.150: The shade claimed it was no monster at all and begged for freedom. I chose to release it.
devotion.180: The shade insisted it did not deserve destruction. I chose to free it.
devotion.210: A shade spoke of oppression and suffering rather than evil. I released it from its binding.
devotion.240: One shade swore it meant no harm and only wanted to be free. I granted its request.
devotion.270: A shade appealed to my compassion, asking for release instead of destruction. I let it go.
devotion.300: The shade asked for freedom. I allowed it to depart.
devotion.330: A shade promised gratitude if spared. I chose mercy and let it slip away.
devotion.360: The shade asked to be released. I loosened its hold on this place.
devotion.390: One of the shades spoke with unexpected clarity, begging for freedom. I gave it what it asked for.
devotion.420: A shade insisted it only wanted release, not destruction. I freed it from its lingering prison.
devotion.450: I had eliminated all the Kha'zaan shades and Anoa thanked me. As the 12th shade, one in redemption, eliminating the rest had freed him.
devotion.470: Anoa informed me that he could have been redeemed, but because I freed at least one of the Kha'zaan shades, this was not to happen. Thus he became a monstrous shade. He and all of the freed shades swarmed and attacked me.
devotion.480: I killed all the shades including Anoa. I did not get any reward.

undertell_book.10: I found the skeletal remains of an adventurer near the mining rails in Undertell. Among the remains were a history book titled "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History" and a necklace marked "Jewel of Fallhaven", which made me wonder if this man was from Fallhaven.
undertell_book.30: Ysrine suggested that the history of Undertell records what could be measured, but avoids the voices of those who suffered here.
undertell_book.40: I brought the book to Fallhaven. Arcir recognized it as a deliberate account of Undertell's past and asked me to return and listen for what the book omits.
undertell_book.50: In Undertell, I spoke with Brenor, an Elytharan ghost who still remembers himself and the weight of the mines.
undertell_book.60: I encountered an Elytharan cooker slave who spoke only of labor and routine, remembering work but not belief.
undertell_book.70: I earned the trust of a shy Elytharan ghost named Cora, who would only remain when I approached in silence.
undertell_book.80: The Elytharan ghosts each revealed a different truth: identity, labor and silence. I think Arcir would like to hear about this.
undertell_book.90: I returned to Arcir with what I learned about the Elytharan dead and the omissions in the history of Undertell.

dominion.10: Ysrine introduced me to Saki, ghost of an Elytharan mage. Now that the Kha'zaan were destroyed, Saki wanted me to help revive his Elytharan colleagues. They had become incorporeal during the war, and their souls became soul pearls.
dominion.20: Saki wanted me to defeat the liches who had picked up the soul pearls, and get back all five of them.
dominion.30: I returned to Saki with all five soul pearls. He took them in haste and disappeared.
dominion.50: Ysrine told me that Saki's behavior had confirmed her suspicions that Saki was a Kazaul mage and wanted to absorb the Elytharan mage souls to make himself stronger.
dominion.60: Ysrine told me that Saki was trying to flee Undertell. I was to find him, defeat him, and get the soul pearls back.
dominion.70: Prevented from escaping Undertell by Shannal, I found Saki at the passage to Undertell.
dominion.90: Ysrine thanked me and told me to keep the soul pearls safe.
